source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH and California county-level official sources reporting West Nile virus human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH publishes weekly WNV surveillance summaries and county-level breakdowns; these are the primary extractable records for confirmed, probable, and neuroinvasive case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET and DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data that may include California August 2024 counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify high-burden California county health department sources (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside) reporting WNV human cases or deaths in August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: California's Central Valley and Southern California counties historically report the highest WNV burden; county-level reports may contain locality-specific extractable records not aggregated at the state level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or international organization summaries (e.g., PAHO, WHO) that cross-reference California WNV human case counts for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to compare against CDPH and county-level collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC Wonder, ProMED, or HealthMap structured data entries for West Nile virus in California during August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured surveillance databases and alert systems provide independently aggregated counts usable for masked validation without contaminating collection.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California WNV case definition documents, surveillance protocol pages, and CDPH methodology notes to support count-semantics interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether reported counts are confirmed, probable, neuroinvasive, or cumulative-vs-weekly is essential for correct field mapping and normalization.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature on California WNV epidemiology in 2024 for case definition and syndrome term context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature may clarify clinical syndrome classifications (WNND, WNF, acute flaccid paralysis) and reporting lag patterns relevant to August 2024 data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering West Nile virus cases or deaths in California in August 2024 as collection support signals.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News reports may surface early outbreak signals, county-specific case announcements, or death confirmations not yet aggregated in official weekly summaries.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources that report only mosquito pool positives, dead bird counts, sentinel chicken seroconversions, or equine/avian cases without human case data for exclusion or human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Per task acceptance contract, non-human case sources must be excluded; ambiguous sources mixing human and vector/animal data require human review before extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with cumulative year-to-date counts that cannot be disaggregated to the August 2024 window for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Reporting periods substantially broader than the task window (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31) require human judgment on whether partial extraction is valid.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus surveillance summaries with human case counts by county, case classification (confirmed/probable/neuroinvasive), deaths, and reporting date. This is the primary authoritative source for California WNV human data.

High-burden county health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, San Bernardino, Riverside, Stanislaus, Tulare) may publish independent WNV human case reports, press releases, or dashboards with locality-level data not available in state aggregates.

CDC ArboNET (Division of Vector-Borne Diseases) publishes national WNV human case surveillance data by state, including California, with neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive breakdowns. Weekly and annual tables may cover August 2024.
PAHO and WHO situation reports may reference US/California WNV case counts as part of regional arboviral surveillance summaries, providing an independent validation layer.
Structured databases including CDC Wonder, ProMED-mail, HealthMap, and California open data portals may contain machine-readable WNV case records for California in August 2024 usable for validation.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV provide case definitions, syndrome classifications, and reporting methodology context essential for correct field normalization.

Reputable news outlets (LA Times, Sacramento Bee, SF Chronicle) and situation reports may publish early WNV case or death announcements citing official sources, providing collection support signals for August 2024.

source_planning_risks.risk: A source intended for validation may leak into collection if roles are not enforced during later discovery.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Keep validation-reserved sources separate until evaluation.

source_planning_risks.risk: Cumulative, annual, newly reported, and suspected counts may be mixed across source categories.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Require evidence quotes and count-semantics fields.
